newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican builders rack up gains on bourse.
newsitem.headline: Mexican builders rack up gains on bourse.

text.p: Infrastructure firms withstood a bout of profit-taking on the Mexican bourse Wednesday, adding to recent gains on hopes for a domestic economic recovery and lucrative foreign contracts.
Builders Grupo Tribasa and Bufete Industrial gained 5.32 percent and 4.83 percent, respectively.
Cement companies Cemex, Cementos Chihuahua and Apasco also shrugged off the bearish market to add to recent gains.
"A lot of investors are now looking at the potential for these companies to get contracts outside of Mexico," said one Mexico City-based construction analyst.
"These are also companies that will benefit from the recovery in the domestic economy," he added.
Tribasa and Bufete are making up for lost ground after having lagged the market recently, while Cemex, ICA and others have outperformed the market, analysts said.

Tribasa, a specialist in toll roads, will be particularly well-positioned to win new contracts in Latin America as governments in the region increasingly allow the private sector to build and operate toll roads, analysts said.
"They recently won some contracts in Chile and are up for one in Ecuador. They are also looking at Argentina and Colombia for new contracts," the Mexico City analyst said.
Grupo Mexicano de Desarrollo, another big Mexican builder, has lagged the market recently and will likely continue to do so on concerns over its debt load, analysts said.

Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo is expected to stress construction during his upcoming State of the Nation address as a means to create jobs, but analysts said they expect few concrete measures to help the industry.
